e: Vision works at Fiona Guthrie's pub until Paladin's mercenaries attack it to capture him, and Fiona is killed in the crossfire.
Vision answers Paladin's summons to his old pub, refuses to be blackmailed over the captive Tommy, and attacks him before leaving.
After selling a man a fake watch, Thomas is shaken by news of Vision, and once he and Lisa outrun the buyer, Paladin snatches him.
Vision walks into Paladin's trap at Saint Mabyn's Psychiatric Sanitarium, frees Tommy, and the two escape by car.
Hiding at a motel, Tommy reboots the dying Vision in its pool, while the Butcherbird Killer corners Paladin in a victim's penthouse.
At Katerina Wells's gala, the Butcherbird Killer unmasks as Jocasta, and Ultron, given Vision's body, tricks her into killing Wells.
Wearing Vision's body, Ultron talks with Tommy at a pub near the gala, and Paladin seizes Tommy a block or two away.
In 1939 Phineas Horton sells the estate to build J.I.M., and now Paladin brings Vision there and the Client's men blow up his van.
Ultron kills Virgil Horton in the house and sends nanobots at London, until Vision talks him down and Tommy and Billy revive Vision.
Paladin's standoff with Vision over Tommy breaks when the Client's Ten Rings attack, and Tommy saves Lisa from Jocasta's nanobot.
Powered by a Wakandan battery, Vision dives into his mind for the source code, frees Lisa from the nanobot, and surrenders to Paladin.
A hooded figure orders the Scarlet Witch to awaken, and Wanda opens her eyes.

notes: Place by place and episode: Edinburgh 1, 2; London 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8; Madripoor 6, 7; Mount Wundagore 8 (existing id wundagore). No new places. Changes to existing entries (after fact-check): Edinburgh #2 and London #2 keep Tommy, since the show first calls him Tommy in episode 2; only London #1 says Thomas. Edinburgh #2 is shortened. Madripoor #6 rewritten: the old text said 'the three' fight off the Ten Rings and then flee the city, but Paladin and E.D.I.T.H. do the fighting with them and they stay in Madripoor into episode 7 (Paladin's hangar). Horton Manor (the Client's drop-off 'just outside of London') is filed under london with sub-place 'The Horton estate, outside London', because the name Horton Manor is never spoken; make it its own place near London if the map needs that. Saint Mabyn's is placed in London on the MCU wiki's word. London #5 is shown through reconstructed CCTV footage of the night before; the pub sits a block or two from Gloucester Road and Clareville Street, per the dialogue. Borough Market as the #1 sub-place rests on the MCU wiki and background signage; the dialogue only says 'the market'. Left out: Roy's Ultimate Electronics (city never given), the cargo plane to Madripoor (#5, in the air), Tajikistan (#6, the Handler's server farm, only spoken of), Studham, Paris and the Louvre (mentioned or Mindspace only), Westview and other archive footage, Billy's New Jersey (#8, reached only through dream-binding; the final trip there is a flight not shown arriving, so no Eastview entry). Episode 8 has no transcript: London #8 and Wundagore #8 rest on the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps, Wikipedia and the MCU wiki location list (Mount Wundagore, Darkhold Castle, in a post-credits scene; the hooded figure is named only off screen).
changes: Name rule: the show first calls him Tommy in episode 2 (Paladin: 'goodbye Tommy', 'Poor Tommy'; he first gives Lisa the name Tommy in the flashback); episode 1 only says Thomas or Tom. So Thomas stays only in London #1, and Tommy is used from #2 on.
Edinburgh #2: shortened from 149 to under 135 characters ('the pub where he used to work' became 'his old pub'), and Thomas changed back to Tommy.

London #1: fixed the order of events: the news report shakes Thomas, then the buyer chases them, then he has a panic attack, and only then does Paladin take him. It does not happen 'just after' the news.
London #2: Thomas changed back to Tommy, which restores the app's current text.
London #3: Thomas changed to Tommy, and 'catches' changed to 'corners' because Paladin escapes the Butcherbird with his drones. Motel kept, since the episode's credits list a Motel Manager.
London #4: kept as is. The episode credits name her Jocasta, and Wikipedia says she reveals herself as Jocasta.
London #5: Thomas changed to Tommy. The pub (three blocks from the gala) and Gloucester Road and Clareville Street are both checked against the transcript.

London #7: Jocasta removed from the capture. The sources only show Paladin delivering Vision to the house, and nothing places Jocasta's body there in episode 7. 'Bomb' changed to 'blow up', since the van is destroyed by an RPG. Reworded to stay under 135 characters. Sub-place now says 'outside London' to match the dialogue ('just outside of London').
London #8: text kept, and the sub-place now also says 'outside London', since the nanobots are sent toward London from the house.
Madripoor #6: Thomas changed to Tommy in both places. Raza says 'Your client is very influential', which supports 'the Client's Ten Rings'.
Madripoor #7: claims check out (the transcript says 'The Wakandans turned it into, like, a alien battery.'). Cut 'own' to bring it from 138 to 134 characters.

Wundagore #8: kept under VisionQuest#8 as an after-credits scene. Laughing Place quotes 'Scarlet Witch, awaken' and says Wanda's eyes open, Wikipedia places it at Mount Wundagore, and the MCU wiki lists Mount Wundagore and Darkhold Castle.

Nothing removed and nothing added. These were checked and left out because they are only mentioned, only memory or footage, or never shown on screen: Madripoor #5 (still on the plane), Tajikistan #6 (spoken only), the New Jersey dream-binding and the final flight in #8 (no arrival shown), and the London hotel in #8 (it falls inside the single London #8 entry).
